calls.summary: Marcus Bell called to book a test drive of the 2026 Kia Telluride SX after comparing trims online. Oscar confirmed local inventory, scheduled a Saturday test drive, and answered his questions on third-row seating and available AWD. Marcus left ready to visit the dealership.

Danielle Prewitt asked about the Sportage Hybrid mpg and available AWD trims. Lila walked her through the hybrid options and booked a test drive for the weekend. Danielle also asked about a possible trade-in on her current sedan.

Gregory Nunn called about renewing his Kia Connect subscription after the free trial ended. Rosey explained the tier pricing and remote start features, then emailed him the renewal link. No dealership visit was scheduled on this call.

First-time caller Priya Raman asked to schedule a test drive of the Kia EV9 and shared her contact details for follow-up. Lee collected her name, phone number, and preferred dealership, then explained the EV9 range and fast charging before booking the test drive. She also asked about lease and financing options.

Anthony Cole called about current lease deals on the K5 GT. Mary reviewed the monthly lease offer, checked available incentives, and scheduled a test drive at his local dealership. Anthony planned to bring a trade-in.
Rebecca Ortiz called to check the delivery status of her ordered Kia Carnival. Sue looked up the build and gave an estimated arrival window along with next steps. No new visit was scheduled.

Kevin Sato was deciding between the Sorento and the Telluride for his growing family. Mike compared seating and towing capacity, then booked a test drive of both at the dealership. Kevin was leaning toward the Telluride.

Laura Kim disputed an extra fee on her Kia Finance America statement. Jennifer reviewed the financing terms, explained the charge, and opened a billing case for review. Laura remained unhappy about the delay.

Derek Foster called about a warranty repair on his Sportage after a dashboard warning light appeared. Rose logged the issue and scheduled a service appointment at his dealership. He was frustrated by the wait time quoted.
Monica Reyes asked about lease terms on the Niro hybrid. Oscar explained the current offer and booked a test drive for her. She mentioned a possible trade-in of her older Kia Soul.
Steven Wu complained that his EV6 delivery had been delayed twice. Lila apologized, checked the transport status, and escalated the case to the dealership manager. Steven wanted a firm delivery date.

Angela Diaz called because her Kia Connect remote start had stopped working. Mary tried troubleshooting steps and opened a support ticket for the app team. Angela was annoyed the app kept logging her out.
Brian Holt called to cancel a pending order and asked about his deposit refund. Lee explained the refund timeline and processing steps. Brian was dissatisfied with the restocking fee.
Teresa Vaughn left a voicemail about a warranty claim on her Sorento transmission. The call rolled to voicemail after hours and no agent answered. A callback was queued for the service department.

Howard Price angrily disputed a duplicate charge on his financing account and threatened to cancel. Rosey struggled to locate the second charge and the call ended unresolved. Howard demanded a manager callback.

prompts.question: Is the customer trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: Yes, the caller is a first-time Kia buyer seeking a fuel-efficient, affordable compact SUV for commuting. They are price-conscious and interested in the Sportage Hybrid as a balance between performance and economy.

prompts.question: What are the customer's expectations?
prompts.answer: The customer expects to see real-world MPG performance and wants to experience how the hybrid drivetrain feels on the road. They are ready to schedule a test drive but need confirmation of appointment timing and dealership location.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: Marcus should have captured the customer's phone number and email at the start of the call rather than allowing the conversation to close without verified contact details. This would ensure dealership follow-up and reduce the risk of no-show for the scheduled test drive.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling Kia America's dealership locator line. My name is Marcus. How can I help you find your next vehicle today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus, yes, I'm interested in learning more about the new Sportage Hybrid. I've been looking at fuel-efficient SUVs and yours keeps coming up.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful. The Sportage Hybrid is an excellent choice, especially with MPG performance in the 40 range depending on driving conditions. To help you best, may I have your first and last name?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Sure, it's Jennifer Martinez.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great, Jennifer. And just to confirm, are you looking to test drive the EX trim, or would you also like to see the SX-Prestige?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: The EX trim sounds perfect for what I need. I want the hybrid features but something practical.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. The EX gives you the hybrid powertrain plus the available all-wheel drive option. Now, what area are you located in, Jennifer? What's your ZIP code?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I'm in the 90210 area, West Los Angeles.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. We have a dealer with excellent inventory in your area. The test drive typically takes about 30 to 45 minutes. Are you available this Saturday afternoon, or would a weekday work better for you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Saturday afternoon would be perfect. What time works?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: We have openings at 2 PM or 3:30 PM. Which would suit your schedule?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: 2 PM is great.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. I've scheduled you for Saturday, October 22nd at 2 PM. Before we wrap up, may I quickly get your best contact number so our dealership can send you confirmation and directions?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: You know what, I'd rather just show up. I have the address on my end already.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I understand. Just know that if anything changes with your appointment, you can call the dealership directly. Is there anything else you'd like to know about the Sportage Hybrid before your visit?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, I think I'm set. Thanks, Marcus.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Jennifer. Thank you for choosing Kia, and we'll see you Saturday at 2 PM. Have a great day.

callDetail.aiSummary: Jennifer Martinez, a first-time Kia prospect from Los Angeles, called to inquire about the Sportage Hybrid EX trim after researching fuel-efficient SUV options. Marcus successfully qualified her interest in the hybrid powertrain and all-wheel drive capabilities, confirmed her service area via ZIP code, and scheduled a test drive appointment for Saturday, October 22nd at 2 PM. However, critical contact information (phone number and email) was not captured, creating a gap in dealership follow-up capability and increasing the risk of a no-show. The call demonstrated strong greeting and close structure but missed opportunity to build customer data for CRM and confirmation messaging.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, well done on your greeting and vehicle qualification. Your tone was warm and you moved Jennifer smoothly through the test drive booking. One coaching point: when Jennifer declined to provide her phone number, you could have offered an alternative like capturing just her email for appointment confirmation and special financing offers. This preserves the customer relationship and reduces no-show risk. Next call, try resetting expectations earlier by saying, 'I'll grab a quick email so our dealership can send you directions and pre-visit details' rather than asking broadly for contact info. Keep up the solid work.

transcript.text: Thank you for calling Kia America, this is Marcus. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?

transcript.text: Hi Marcus, my name is Danielle Reyes. I'm just starting to look at three-row SUVs for our family and wanted some info.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful, Danielle. Congratulations on the search. Are you looking to seat the whole family, and do you have a sense of gas versus hybrid or electric?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: We've got three kids, so we need the third row. Probably gas for now, but I'm curious about the electric one too.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. For a family of five the Kia Telluride is our most popular three-row. It seats up to eight, has a 291-horsepower V6, and available all-wheel drive. If you want to go electric, the EV9 is the three-row equivalent.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: The Telluride keeps coming up. What does one of those actually run these days?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: The Telluride starts right around thirty-seven thousand, and it climbs with the premium trims. The EV9 begins closer to fifty-five thousand before any incentives.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay, honestly I want to keep this manageable. We were also over at the Honda store looking at the Pilot, and they quoted us something pretty aggressive.

transcript.text: That's a fair comparison. Where the Telluride tends to win people over is the standard features and the interior quality at that price. We also have Kia Finance America running promotional rates this month, so we can often land the monthly payment where you need it.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That helps. One thing though, I don't want to feel locked into some long term commitment if our situation changes.

transcript.text: Completely understand. We have flexible lease terms as well as traditional financing, so you're not boxed in. A lease can actually give you the shortest commitment if that's a concern.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Good to know. I'd really want to sit in both before deciding anything, and my husband needs to be there too.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's exactly what I'd recommend. Let's get you and your husband a test drive so you can compare the Telluride and the EV9 side by side. What day works best for you both?

transcript.text: Thursday would work, sometime in the morning. We're hoping to decide before the end of the month though.

transcript.text: Thursday morning it is. I have a ten o'clock test drive open at your local dealership, and I'll have both vehicles pulled up and ready. That leaves plenty of time to decide this month.

transcript.text: Perfect, Thursday at ten works for us.

qaPairs.question: How much does the Kia Telluride cost?
qaPairs.answer: The Telluride starts around $37,000 and pricing varies by trim and options. Let's set up a test drive so a product specialist can walk you through exact figures and current offers.

qaPairs.question: What is the range on the Kia EV9?
qaPairs.answer: The EV9 offers up to roughly 300 miles of range depending on trim, along with fast charging. I'd love to book you a test drive so you can experience it firsthand.

qaPairs.question: Do you have any lease deals right now?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we have promotional lease and APR offers through Kia Finance America that change monthly. Share your ZIP and preferred model and I'll set you up with a specialist to review the latest deals.

qaPairs.question: What is the difference between the Sorento and the Telluride?
qaPairs.answer: Both are three-row SUVs, with the Sorento being a bit more compact and value-focused and the Telluride offering more space and premium trims. A test drive of both is the best way to compare, shall I schedule one?

qaPairs.question: Does the Sportage come as a hybrid?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, the Sportage Hybrid delivers around 40-plus mpg with an available dual-motor AWD option. Let's book a test drive so you can feel the difference for yourself.

qaPairs.question: How fast can the EV6 charge?
qaPairs.answer: The EV6 uses an 800V system for ultra-fast charging that can add significant range in minutes at a compatible station. I can arrange a test drive so a specialist can show you the charging details.

qaPairs.question: What is the starting price of the Kia Soul?
qaPairs.answer: The Soul starts around $21,000 and offers distinctive styling with generous headroom. Would you like to schedule a test drive to see it in person?

qaPairs.question: Is the K4 replacing the Forte?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, the K4 is the compact sedan that replaces the Forte, with modern tech and a roomy interior. Let's set up a test drive so you can check out the updates.

qaPairs.question: Do you sell certified pre-owned Kias?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our dealers carry certified pre-owned Kias that go through a thorough inspection and include added coverage. Share your ZIP and I'll connect you with a nearby dealer to view inventory.

qaPairs.question: What financing options do you offer?
qaPairs.answer: Kia Finance America offers both financing and leasing with promotional APR and lease offers. A specialist can review the best fit for you during your visit, want me to book it?

qaPairs.question: How many seats does the Carnival have?
qaPairs.answer: The Carnival MPV seats up to 8 with sliding doors and an available hybrid option. Let's schedule a test drive so you can experience the family-friendly cabin.

qaPairs.question: What is Kia Connect?
qaPairs.answer: Kia Connect is our connected-car service with remote start, vehicle status, navigation, and emergency assistance, starting with a free trial. I can have a specialist explain the tiers when you come in for a test drive.

qaPairs.question: Which Kia SUV is best for families?
qaPairs.answer: Families often love the Telluride and Sorento for three-row space, or the EV9 for an electric option. The best way to decide is a test drive, shall I set one up?

qaPairs.question: Does the Seltos come with all-wheel drive?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, the Seltos offers available AWD and a turbo engine option in a spacious subcompact package. Let's book a test drive so you can take it out on the road.

qaPairs.question: What is the fuel economy on the Niro?
qaPairs.answer: The Niro comes in HEV, PHEV, and EV variants and delivers high fuel economy across the lineup. I'd be happy to schedule a test drive so a specialist can match the right variant to your driving.

qaPairs.question: Do you have the K5 with all-wheel drive?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, the K5 midsize sedan offers available AWD along with a sporty GT turbo trim. Share your ZIP and I'll find a dealer with one available for a test drive.

qaPairs.question: How do I find a Kia dealer near me?
qaPairs.answer: I can help with that right now, just share your ZIP code and I'll confirm the nearest dealer and set up your test drive.

qaPairs.question: Can I build and price a Kia online?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, you can configure your ideal Kia and a specialist can confirm exact pricing and offers when you visit. Would you like me to schedule a test drive to finalize the details?

qaPairs.question: Is the EV9 eligible for any incentives?
qaPairs.answer: Available EV incentives can vary by model, trim, and location, and they change over time. Let's book a test drive so a specialist can review current EV offers with you.

qaPairs.question: How long does a test drive take?
qaPairs.answer: A test drive typically takes about 30 to 45 minutes, including time to review features and offers. Let me grab your ZIP and preferred day and I'll get it scheduled.
